text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: elevated 5xx rate (gateway timeouts / 504) impacting Private/VPC peered customers in us-west-2. Triggered by >3% error rate on inference-gateway. Paging oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: I'm on it. seeing spike at 11:02 UTC. emergency dashboard shows gateway 504s clustered to instances hitting peering tunnels to customer VPCs. ETA 5.

eng-network-jess: I see unusual BGP withdraws from one transit peer to our peering appliance starting 11:01:12. Could be route-filter in the new peering policy rollout. Rolling back the filter now.

eng-runtime-raja: Any customer-facing mitigation we can do while network works the rollback? We can failover traffic to public egress for affected routes.

oncall-sre: Raja yes — can we change routing policy for the inference-gateway service to prefer public egress for the customer set, for a quick fallback? Keep TTLs low.

eng-runtime-raja: I can flip the policy. Doing `redwood route set preference --service inference-gateway --scope private-peers --prefer public-egress --exp 30m` now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: route-preference-v1 -> canary -> 3 nodes

eng-network-jess: Confirmed: I accidentally pushed a prefix-length filter in the peering policy that removed /24s for two customer prefixes. Rolling that commit back: `git revert 5f3a9b2` and applying. Pushing policy to peering appliance.

eng-network-jess: Running `show bgp neighbors 10.200.1.1 advertised-routes` shows the /24s re-advertised to the peer. Waiting for converge.

eng-sre-marta: Can someone tail the gateway logs for retries? `kubectl logs -l app=inference-gateway -c proxy --since=2m` — I'm seeing increased 502 and 504 with `upstream connection timed out`.

oncall-sre: tailing logs. sample:
```
[11:03:05] proxy ERROR upstream connection timed out while connecting to 10.200.5.23:504
[11:03:06] proxy WARN retry attempt 1 for request id=abcd-1234
```

eng-network-jess: BGP looks stable now, peers re-advertised. But conntrack on transit appliance is showing a spike. `conntrack -S` shows ephemeral exhaustion risk. NAT gateway ephemeral ports might be depleted if we keep falling back to public egress.

eng-runtime-raja: Good catch. We should throttle retries at gateway to avoid conntrack exhaustion. Pushing a temporary rate-limit: `set-config inference-gateway retry.max=2 retry.backoff=250ms`.

platform-oncall-oliver: I'm increasing NAT gateway ephemeral port pool for the transit appliance and adding a second NAT instance in the private subnet to spread state. Doing cloud console changes now.

cust-success-lina: Heads-up — two customers (acct-1423 and acct-8810) reported elevated errors on their end. I'm drafting a short notice saying we're actively mitigating and will follow up with impact window.

oncall-sre: After rollback + route-fallback + NAT scale we see 504 rate drop from 3.4% -> 0.6% in 6 minutes. Continuing to monitor.

eng-network-jess: Post-rollback, double-checked peering ACLs — there was a stray policy that blocked TCP ports >1024 for one peer (bad filter). Removed it. Also added a guard in our CI that prevents prefix-length filtering for active customer prefixes.

eng-sre-marta: Rolling post-incident tasks: capture conntrack histogram, record peak ephemeral allocation, and correlate with retry patterns from gateway. I'll add unit in runbook.

oncall-sre: TL;DR: Root cause was accidental route/prefix filter in peering policy rollout which caused asymmetric/partial withdrawal -> gateway retries -> NAT ephemeral port pressure -> 504s. Mitigations: rollback filter, route preference fallback to public egress, throttle gateway retries, scale NAT pool.

cust-success-lina: Sent interim message to affected customers: "We detected a networking configuration issue affecting private peering traffic. Mitigations are in place; error rates are returning to normal. We'll follow up with a full post-incident summary." :email:

eng-runtime-raja: Can we keep the fallback route preference for 30m then auto-revert? deploy-bot set expansion to 30m earlier. I recommend 1h to be safe.

oncall-sre: Set to 60m. `redwood route update --id route-preference-v1 --exp 60m` applied.

platform-oncall-oliver: NAT pool increased, second NAT attached. Monitoring conntrack usage; currently down from 98% to 34%.

eng-network-jess: Added temporary BGP session dampening thresholds and a CI check for peering policy diffs. Will open PR for a rollout gating test.

eng-sre-marta: I'll own the postmortem. Assigning follow-up actions: network policy CI gate (jess), gateway retry tuning permanent change (raja), runbook update + conntrack observability (marta), customer impact timeline and postmortem note (lina).

oncall-sre: Good work team. Leaving an oncall handoff note for next shift. Final status at 11:24 UTC: errors returned to baseline, mitigation in place, postmortem assigned.

cust-success-lina: I'll attach the list of impacted accounts to the postmortem and coordinate outreach.

eng-network-jess: FYI command snippets I used:
```
# show advertised prefixes
show bgp neighbors 10.200.1.1 advertised-routes | grep 198.51
# conntrack snapshot
conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
# revert peering policy
git revert 5f3a9b2 && ci/deploy-peering-policy.sh
```

oncall-sre: Closing thread for now. Please add any additional notes to the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
